source.title: Scaling can lead to compositional generalization
source.authors: Florian Redhardt; Yassir Akram; Simon Schug

record.tranche_reason: It tests whether scaling model or training-task size improves held-out task performance, but on synthetic compositional tasks rather than language-model pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The paper's scaling experiments measure compositional generalization on held-out synthetic tasks, not held-out cross-entropy loss or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Its image-generation experiments compare compositional success and constituent decoding across models, but do not scale those models or test a loss power law. Values for the relevant scaling results are shown in figures; the text gives qualitative descriptions.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. It trains small MLPs and a 4-layer transformer directly on synthetic compositional tasks and reports held-out R² or accuracy as training-task count and model size grow. There is no language-model pretraining, no held-out pretraining loss, no power-law or other fit, no extrapolation, and no downstream prediction from scale or loss. V6 names downstream performance of pretrained language models improving predictably, so these results do not match it; they also do not show the power-law form that V5 requires. Kaplan and Hoffmann are cited only as motivation. The scaling finding is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also prove that MLPs can approximate hyperteachers with neurons linear in the number of modules. They show that linear decodability of task constituents correlates with text-to-image composition success across four diffusion models. They stress that not all scaling helps: training support must cover the task space.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies compositional generalization in synthetic task families and image-generation models, scaling task coverage or model size; it does not fit language-model loss power laws or estimate compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Compositional generalization depends on training-task coverage: the authors report failures with non-compositional or disconnected support and with rarely encountered modules. They report that adequate coverage is required.

fits_no_version.finding: In synthetic compositional task families, held-out compositional generalization (R²/accuracy) rises toward ceiling as training-task count and MLP size grow. This holds only with compositional and connected training support; the training tasks needed grow sub-exponentially in total tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling training-task coverage and model size yields compositional generalization in standard networks trained directly on synthetic compositional tasks, conditional on training-support coverage.

record.problems: The scaling evidence relevant to V6 is on synthetic compositional tasks, not standard downstream language-model benchmarks. Most scale-result values are presented in figures rather than stated numerically in the text. The authors note that theoretical conditions guaranteeing stochastic gradient descent finds the generalizing solution remain open.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results relevant to V6 were left out. Image-generation experiments compare compositional success and constituent decoding across models, but do not test model scaling or a loss-scaling relationship.

untested.parts: All: no LM pretraining loss versus N, D or C.
All: depth and width varied with total size, not at fixed parameter count, and not on LM loss.
No power-law fits in any modality. Image models are compared but not scaled.
No pretrained LM downstream tasks; no predictive relation to scale or loss.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'supports' label is removed because the system (non-pretrained small networks on synthetic tasks) and the measure (qualitative improvement, no predictive law) do not match V6. All scaling values are figure-only.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power-law fits from small language-model runs predict much larger runs.
The compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its dependence on compute.
Architecture changes at fixed parameter count and their effect on language-model loss.
Whether the same loss power law holds across modalities or training regimes.

The paper evaluates held-out compositional task performance in synthetic task families; it does not test conventional downstream language-model benchmarks, performance as a function of pretraining loss, or predictive fits for downstream scores.
Dependence of language-model loss exponents or compute-optimal splits on fitting choices, and whether such loss curves bend away from power laws.

rows.subject: multilayer perceptron (hyperteacher task family)
rows.size_stated: Model size varied; default architecture has four hidden layers with 1024 hidden neurons each.
rows.operation_detail: Scaled the number of training tasks by varying the number of modules.
rows.note: The text reports that compositional generalization improves as the number of training tasks is scaled; values are not stated in text.
rows.check: Synthetic hyperteacher MLP trained directly on tasks, not a pretrained LM's downstream score; no predictive fit. Does not bear on V6. State reflects the paper's own qualitative improvement (figure only).

rows.subject: multilayer perceptron (hyperteacher task family)
rows.size_stated: Model size varied; default architecture has four hidden layers with 1024 hidden neurons each.
rows.operation_detail: Scaled the number of training tasks by varying the number of task components.
rows.note: The text reports that compositional generalization improves as the number of training tasks is scaled; values are not stated in text.
rows.check: Same as r1: training-task scaling via K on synthetic tasks; not V6's system or measure.

rows.subject: multilayer perceptron (hyperteacher task family)
rows.size_stated: Model size varied; default architecture has four hidden layers with 1024 hidden neurons each.
rows.operation_detail: Changed the fraction of tasks held out from training, thereby varying the training-task count.
rows.note: The text reports that compositional generalization improves as the number of training tasks is scaled; values are not stated in text.
rows.check: Same as r1. Improvement comes from decreasing the held-out fraction, i.e. more training tasks.

rows.subject: multilayer perceptron (hyperteacher task family)
rows.size_stated: Varied hidden-layer width and number of hidden layers.
rows.operation_detail: Increased model size by varying hidden-layer size and depth.

conditions.value: multiple encodings; Figure 2 shows identity, orthogonal, language, invertible NN, interval shuffle, and few shot

rows.note: The text states that increasing model size consistently improves compositional generalization given sufficient data, across the displayed task encodings.
rows.check: Model-size scaling of an MLP on synthetic tasks, qualified by 'given sufficient data'. Qualitative only, with no power-law fit; not LM downstream performance.

rows.subject: multilayer perceptron (compositional preference task family)
rows.operation_detail: Scaled the number of training tasks by varying task-family size, task components, and the fraction held out.
rows.note: The authors state that the data-scaling result is reproduced on this task family; the figure presents multiple task-scale conditions.
rows.check: Grid-world compositional preference tasks trained directly; not LM downstream performance.

rows.subject: multilayer perceptron (compositional preference task family)
rows.size_stated: Model size varied by hidden-neuron count and number of hidden layers.
rows.note: The authors state that scaling model size reproduces the main finding on this task family.
rows.check: Same as r5, for model size; the few-shot encoding was not evaluated.

rows.subject: decoder-only transformer (hyperteacher task family)
rows.size_stated: 4 layers, 4 attention heads, model dimension 256, feedforward dimension 1024.
rows.operation_detail: Scaled training-task count by varying task-family size and the fraction of tasks held out.
rows.note: The text says data scaling leads to compositional generalization in the transformer and that it needs fewer training tasks than the MLP to reach R² > 0.95.
rows.check: Small transformer trained on the synthetic task, not a pretrained LM. The comparison of training tasks needed versus the MLP is an architecture contrast.

rows.subject: multilayer perceptron with a deep hyperteacher task family
rows.size_stated: The task network has three hidden layers, each with 16 hidden neurons.
rows.operation_detail: Scaled training-task count by varying task-family size, task components, and the fraction held out.
rows.note: The text says this reproduces the data-scaling finding, while noting that the deeper task network makes the task noticeably more difficult.
rows.check: Deep hyperteacher variant; not LM downstream performance.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Held-out compositional task performance in the tested synthetic task families and architectures
reader_labels.reason: The authors report improved compositional generalization with more training tasks or larger models in the tested settings (r1–r8); the paper does not establish a quantitative predictive law for conventional downstream tasks.
